**Commentary on Surah al-Rum**

Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

These verses were revealed when Sabur (Shapur), king of the Persians, defeated the Romans in the lands of al-Sham (the Levant), in the districts of al-Jazirah adjoining it, and in the distant parts of the Roman lands. He forced Heraclius (Hiraql), king of the Romans, until he drove him to Constantinople (al-Qustantiniyyah) and besieged him there for a long time. Then the dynasty returned to Heraclius, as will come later.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr related to us, Abu Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land﴾. He said: "They were defeated and they defeated [others]." He said: "The polytheists (al-mushrikun) loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, because they were people of idols, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, they will be victorious.'" Abu Bakr mentioned that to them, and they said: "Set between us and you a term: if we prevail, we will have such-and-such, and if you prevail, you will have such-and-such." So he set a term of five years, but they did not prevail. Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Why did you not make it less than that?" I think he said: "Ten." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The bid' (a few) is less than ten." Then the Romans prevailed after that. He said: "That is His saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾."

This was related in the same way by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, both from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib (a good hadith with a single transmission route). We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan, from Habib."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir related it:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id, or Sa'id Abu Sa'd al-Tha'labi, who is called Abu Sa'd, from the people of Tarsus, related to us Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, and he mentioned it. In their version: Sufyan said: "It reached me that they were defeated on the day of Badr."

Another hadith: Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash related from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "Five have passed: the smoke (al-Dukhan), the inevitable punishment (al-Lizam), the great assault (al-Batshah), the moon (al-Qamar), and the Romans." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' related to us, al-Muharibi related to us, from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, that is al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Persia was dominant over the Romans, and the polytheists loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book and were closer to their religion. When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, they said: 'O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will prevail over Persia within a few years?!' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you bet with us on that?' So they made a wager with him for four she-camels up to seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened. The polytheists rejoiced at that, and it grieved the Muslims. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'What is a few years in your view?' They said: 'Less than ten.' He said: 'Go, increase the stakes for them and add two years to the term.' He said: 'The two years had not passed before riders came with news of the Romans' victory over Persia, and the believers rejoiced at that. Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ up to His saying: ﴿[the promise of Allah] Allah does not fail His promise﴾."

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Wakili related to us, Mu'ammal related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, the polytheists said to Abu Bakr: 'Do you not see what your companion says? He claims that the Romans will overcome Persia.' He said: 'My companion spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you like us to wager with you?' So he set a term between himself and them, but the term expired before the Romans overcame Persia. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and it displeased and disturbed him. He said to Abu Bakr: 'What prompted you to this?' He said: 'Confirmation of Allah and His Messenger.' He said: 'Go to them, increase the stake, and make the term a few years.' Abu Bakr came to them and said: 'Would you like to renew it, for renewal is better?' They said: 'Yes.' [He said:] The years had not passed before the Romans overcame Persia. They tied their horses in Madain (al-Mada'in), and they built al-Rumiyyah. Abu Bakr brought the winnings to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'This is unlawful gain.' He said: 'Give it in charity.'"

Another hadith: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Uways related to us, Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Nayyar ibn Mukram al-Aslami, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, Persia on the day this verse was revealed was dominating the Romans. The Muslims loved the victory of the Romans over them, because they and the Romans were People of the Book. Allah's saying concerning that is: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾. The Quraysh loved the victory of Persia, because they and the Persians were not People of the Book and did not believe in resurrection. When Allah revealed this verse, Abu Bakr went out crying in the outskirts of Makkah: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾. Some people of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: 'That is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will overcome Persia within a few years. Shall we wager you on that?' He said: 'Yes,' and that was before the prohibition of gambling. Abu Bakr and the polytheists placed stakes and agreed on the wager. They said to Abu Bakr: 'How many years do you set for the bid': three to nine years? Name a middle term between us and you, which we will reach.' He said: 'They set six years between them.' He said: 'The six years passed before they prevailed, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's pledge. When the seventh year arrived, the Romans prevailed over Persia.' The Muslims blamed Abu Bakr for naming six years. He said: 'Because Allah said: ﴿within a few years﴾.' He said: 'At that, many people embraced Islam.'"

This is how al-Tirmidhi related it, and then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith (good and authentic). We only know it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad. A similar report has been transmitted as mursal (with a gap in the chain), from a group of the Successors (tabi'un), such as 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Zuhri, and others."

Among the strangest of these accounts is what Imam Sunayd ibn Da'ud related in his tafsir, where he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "In Persia there was a woman who bore only kings and heroes. Kisra summoned her and said: 'I want to send an army to the Romans and appoint over them one of your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint.' She said: 'This one, so-and-so, is more cunning than a fox and more wary than a falcon. This one, Farkhan, is more penetrating than a spear. And this one, Shahriyaraz, is more forbearing than such-and-such,' meaning her three sons. 'Appoint whichever of them you wish.' He said: 'I have appointed the forbearing one.' So he appointed Shahriyaraz, who marched against the Romans with the people of Persia, prevailed over them, killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I related this hadith to 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and he said: 'Have you not seen the lands of al-Sham?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'If you had seen them, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down.' Then I went to al-Sham afterward and saw it." Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir from the route of Sunayd.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: Yahya ibn Ya'mar related to me that Caesar (Qaysar) sent a man called Qitmah with an army of Romans, and Kisra sent Shahriyaraz. They met at Adhru'at and Busra, which is the nearest part of al-Sham to you. Persia met the Romans and defeated them. The disbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims disliked it.

'Ikrimah said: "The polytheists met the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are unlettered. Our brothers from the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers from the People of the Book. If you fight us, we will surely prevail over you.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome. Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills﴾. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the disbelievers and said: 'Do you rejoice at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and may Allah not gladden your eyes. By Allah, Allah will surely give the Romans victory over Persia; our Prophet (ﷺ) told us of that.' Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up to him and said: 'You have lied, O Abu Fudayl.' Abu Bakr said to him: 'You are the greater liar, O enemy of Allah.' He said: 'I will wager you ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans prevail over Persia, I will pay, and if Persia prevails, you will pay, within three years.' Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'That is not how I mentioned it. The bid' is only what lies between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term.' Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy and said: 'Perhaps you regret it?' He said: 'No, come, I will increase the stake for you and extend the term. Make it a hundred she-camels for a hundred she-camels, up to nine years.' He said: 'I have done so.' Then the Romans prevailed over Persia before that time, and the Muslims were victorious."

Ikrimah said: When Persia prevailed over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and he was the brother of Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. He said to his companions: "I saw myself sitting on the throne of Kisra." This reached Kisra, and he wrote to Shahrayaz: "When my letter reaches you [[Addition from F.]], send me the head of Farkhan." Shahrayaz wrote back: "O King, you will not find another like Farkhan. He has force and a reputation among the enemy, so do not do this." Kisra wrote: "Among the men of Persia there are successors to him, so hasten to send me his head." Shahrayaz returned the matter to him, and Kisra became angry and did not answer him. He sent a courier to the people of Persia: "I have removed [[In F: "dismissed".]] Shahrayaz from you and appointed Farkhan over you." Then he gave the courier a small, delicate document and said: "When Farkhan takes power and his brother submits to him, give him this." When Shahrayaz read the letter, he said: "I hear and obey," and he got down from his throne, and Farkhan sat down, and Shahrayaz handed him the document. Farkhan said [[In F: "Then he said".]]: "Bring Shahrayaz to me," and had him brought forward to strike his neck. Shahrayaz said: "Do not hurry with me until I write my will." He said: "Yes." So he called for the chest, and Shahrayaz was given the pages [[In T, F, A: "three pages".]], and Farkhan said: "Kisra and I have gone back and forth over all this, and you wanted to kill me with a single letter." The king returned to his brother Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. Then Shahrayaz wrote to Qaysar, king of the Romans: "I have a need of you that neither the post-riders nor the pages can carry, so meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, and I will meet you with fifty Persians." Qaysar came with five hundred thousand Romans and placed spies before him along the road, fearing that he had been deceived, until his spies informed him that there were only fifty men with him. Then cushions were spread for the two of them, and they met in a brocade tent that had been pitched for them, each of them with a knife. They summoned an interpreter between them, and Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]] said: "Those who ruined your cities are I and my brother, through our cunning and our bravery. Kisra envied us, and he wanted me to kill my brother, but I refused, and then he ordered my brother to kill me. We have both deposed him, and so we are fighting him with you." He said: "You have done right." Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two, and if it passes two it spreads. He said: "Indeed." So they both killed the interpreter with their knives. Then God destroyed Kisra, and news of this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, and he rejoiced, and the Muslims rejoiced with him.

This is a strange narrative and a remarkable structure. Let us now discuss the words of these noble verses. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾, the discussion of the disjointed letters at the beginning of the surahs has already been given at the start of Surah al-Baqarah. As for the Romans (al-Rum), they are of the lineage of al-Is ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and they are cousins of the Children of Israel, and they are called the Sons of the Yellow (Banu al-Asfar). They followed the religion of the Greeks (al-Yunan), and the Greeks are of the lineage of Yafith ibn Nuh, paternal cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are called "the perplexed," and they prayed toward the North Pole. They are the ones who founded Damascus and built its temple, and in it there are prayer niches facing north. The Romans remained upon their religion until about three hundred years before the sending of the Messiah. The one who ruled Syria together with the Jazirah among them was called Qaysar. The first of the kings to enter the religion of the Christians was Constantine ibn Qastas, and his mother was Maryam al-Haylaniyyah al-Shadqaniyyah [[In T: "al-Qandaqaniyyah"; in F: "al-Ghandaqaniyyah".]] from the land of Harran. She had been a Christian before him, and she invited him to her religion. He had previously been a philosopher, so he followed her, it is said, out of dissimulation (taqiyyah). The Christians gathered around him, and in his time they debated with Abdullah ibn Aryus, and they differed in a widespread, scattered disagreement that could not be controlled. Yet three hundred and eighteen bishops from their assembly agreed, and they set down for Constantine the creed, which they call the Great Trust, though it is in fact the Base Betrayal. They also wrote for him the canons, meaning the books of rulings containing permitted and forbidden matters and other things they needed, and they altered the religion of the Messiah, peace be upon him, adding to it and subtracting from it. They went off toward the East, replaced the Sabbath with Sunday, worshipped the cross, and made the pig lawful. They instituted festivals that they invented, such as the feast of the Cross, the Qiddas, the Ghitas, and other innovations, the Bawa'ith and the Sha'anin, and they made the Pope their chief, then the Patriarchs, then the Metropolitans, then the Bishops and presbyters, then the deacons. They invented monasticism. The king built churches and temples for them, and he founded the city named after him, which is Constantinople. It is said that in his days he built twelve thousand churches, and he built Bethlehem with three prayer niches, and his mother built the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. These are the Melkites, meaning those who follow the religion of the king.

Then after them came the Jacobites, followers of Yaqub al-Iskaf, then the Nestorians, the companions of Nestora. They are many sects and groups, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They have split into seventy-two sects." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4596, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 3992. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "The chain of Awf ibn Malik has some criticism, and Rashid ibn Sa'd, Abu Hatim said of him: truthful. Abbad ibn Yusuf was narrated from only by Ibn Majah, and he has no other hadith in my view except this one; Ibn Adi said: he narrated hadiths that he alone transmitted. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and the rest of the men of the chain are trustworthy."]] The point is that they persisted in Christianity: whenever a Qaysar died, another succeeded him, until the last of them was Heraclius. He was one of the wisest of men, the most resolute and shrewd of kings, the deepest in insight and the most far-sighted in judgment. He ruled over them with great authority and great dignity. Kisra, king of the Persians, opposed him. Kisra ruled the lands such as Iraq, Khurasan, al-Rayy, and all the lands of the non-Arabs, and he was Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf. His kingdom was wider than the kingdom of Qaysar, and he had the leadership of the non-Arabs and the folly of the Persians. They were Magians who worshipped fire. It has been mentioned earlier from Ikrimah that he sent his deputies and his army to him, and they fought him. The well-known account is that Kisra himself invaded him in his lands, overpowered him, broke him, and humbled him, until nothing remained with him except the city of Constantinople. He besieged it for a long time until it grew tight for him. The Christians revered him exceedingly, and Kisra was unable to conquer the city, nor was it possible for him to do so because of its strength, since half of it lies on the land side and half on the sea side, and provisions and reinforcements kept reaching them from there. When the matter dragged on, Qaysar devised a stratagem and thought up a deception, so he asked Kisra to withdraw from his lands in exchange for money as a settlement, and he would stipulate whatever he wished. Kisra agreed to this and demanded from him enormous wealth, such as no king of the world could provide: gold, jewels, fabrics, slave girls, servants, and many kinds of goods. Qaysar complied and led him to believe that he had all that was requested. The pretense seemed small to him because of what was demanded, and had he and Kisra combined their power, they would have been unable to gather a tenth of it. He asked Kisra to allow him to go out to the lands of Syria and the regions of his kingdom to seek to collect this from his treasuries, storehouses, and hoards, and Kisra released him. When Qaysar resolved to leave Constantinople, he gathered the people of his religion and said: "I am going out on a matter I have settled, with a force I have chosen from my army. If I return to you before the year is out, I will be your king, and if I do not return to you before it, you have the choice: if you wish, continue in my allegiance, and if you wish, appoint someone other than me over you." They answered: "You are our king as long as you live, even if you are absent for ten years." When he left Constantinople, he set out lightly with a moderate army, while Kisra was camped around Constantinople waiting for him to return. Qaysar immediately mounted and marched swiftly until he reached the land of Persia, and he ravaged their lands, killing their men and the fighters among them, step by step, and he kept on killing until he reached al-Mada'in, which was the capital of Kisra's kingdom. He killed those in it, took all his stores and wealth, captured his women and harem, shaved the head of his son, mounted him on a donkey, and sent with him some of his own people, the Asawira, in utmost humiliation and abasement. He wrote to Kisra: "This is what you asked for, so take it." When this reached Kisra, grief overcame him to a degree that only God, Mighty and Majestic, can count, and his rage against the city intensified. He pressed hard in besieging it with every possible means, but he could not manage it. When he failed, he rode to block the road for him at the ford of the Jayhun, the only route by which Qaysar could reach Constantinople. When Qaysar learned of this, he devised a great stratagem unprecedented in its kind: he stationed his army and his stores with him at the mouth of the ford, rode out with part of the army, and ordered loads of straw, dung, and manure to be carried with him. He advanced upstream in the water for nearly a day, then ordered those loads to be thrown into the river. When they passed by Kisra, he and his army thought that they had crossed there, so they rode in pursuit of them, and the ford was left clear of the Persians. Qaysar came and ordered them to rise and enter the crossing, so they crossed and hurried their march, and they outpaced Kisra and his armies and entered Constantinople. That was a day remembered among the Christians, and Kisra and his armies remained bewildered, not knowing what to do. They had not gained the lands of Qaysar, while their own lands had been ravaged by the Romans, who had taken their stores and taken captive their offspring and women. So this was the Romans' victory over Persia, and it came nine years after the Persians' victory over the Romans.

The battle between Persia and the Romans, in which the Romans were defeated, took place between Adhruat and Busra, as reported by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. It is the frontier of the lands of Syria on the side adjoining the lands of the Hijaz.

Mujahid said: That happened in al-Jazirah, which is the nearest of the lands of the Romans to Persia. And God knows best.

Then the Romans defeated the Persians after a few years, and "a few years" means nine. In the Arabic language, *al-bidh'* (a few) refers to any number from three to nine. This is also what is related in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and others, through 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jumahi, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr during his pledge of allegiance [[In T: "mubayi'atihi" (his pledge of allegiance).]]: "Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated." (He said:) "Did you not take precaution, O Abu Bakr? Indeed, *al-bidh'* is between three and nine." Then he said: "This is a good, strange hadith from this route." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3191, and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/12).]]

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr that he said the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/16).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾, meaning: before that and after it. It is built on a *damm* (vowel) because the noun it modifies was cut off from the genitive construction, which is His saying *qabl* (before), with its implied complement intended.

﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah﴾, meaning: the Romans, the companions of Caesar, king of the Levant, over the Persians, the companions of Khosrow, who were Magians. The Roman victory over the Persians took place on the day of the Battle of Badr, according to a great number of scholars, such as Ibn 'Abbas, al-Thawri, al-Suddi and others. It has also been related in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bazzar, through al-A'mash, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When it was the day of Badr, the Romans prevailed over the Persians, and that pleased the believers and made them happy. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3192, and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/16).]]

Others said: Rather, the Roman victory over the Persians was in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. This was said by 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others. Some of them justified this view by saying that Caesar had vowed that if Allah granted him victory over Khosrow, he would walk from Homs to Iliya, which is Bayt al-Maqdis, in gratitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He did so. When he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, he did not leave it until there came to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he had sent with Dihya ibn Khalifa. Dihya gave it to the governor of Busra, and the governor of Busra delivered it to Caesar. When it reached him, he asked about the Arabs of Hijaz who were in the Levant. Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb al-Umawi was brought to him, along with a group of the Quraysh disbelievers who were in Gaza. They were brought to him and sat before him. He said: "Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?" Abu Sufyan said: "I am." He said to his companions, whom he had seated behind him: "I am going to ask this man about this man. If he lies, then contradict him." Abu Sufyan said: "By Allah, had it not been that they would have reported me as a liar, I would have lied." Heraclius asked him about his lineage and description. Among what he asked was: "Does he break his promises?" I said: "No. And we are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it," meaning the truce that had been concluded between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Quraysh disbelievers on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, to suspend hostilities between them for ten years. From this they inferred that the Roman victory over the Persians took place in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, because Caesar fulfilled his vow only after al-Hudaybiyah. And Allah knows best.

The proponents of the first view could respond to this by saying that his land had been ruined and disordered, so he was not able to fulfil his vow until he had restored what needed restoring and attended to his lands. Then, four years after his victory, he fulfilled his vow. And Allah knows best.

The matter in this is simple and near, except that when the Persians prevailed over the Romans, that grieved the believers, and when the Romans prevailed over the Persians, the believers rejoiced at that, because the Romans were in general a people of the Book, so they were closer to the believers than the Magians. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears from what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 82–83]. And Allah, the Exalted, said here: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Safwan related to us, al-Walid related to us, Usayd al-Kilabi related to me, who said: "I heard al-'Ala' ibn al-Zubayr al-Kilabi relate from his father, who said: 'I saw the Persians overcome the Romans, then I saw the Romans overcome the Persians, then I saw the Muslims overcome both the Persians and the Romans, all within fifteen years.'" [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim related from" (instead of "I heard").]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, meaning: in His victory and in His retribution against His enemies; ﴿the Merciful﴾, toward His believing servants.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah's promise. Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, meaning: this which We have informed you of, O Muhammad, that We will grant victory to the Romans over the Persians, is a promise from Allah that is true, and a true report that cannot be broken, and it must come to pass and occur. This is because Allah's custom is to grant victory to the nearer of the two fighting groups to the truth, and to make the final outcome theirs. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾, meaning: the wisdom of Allah in His creation and His actions, which are firm and proceed in accordance with justice.

* *

His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾, meaning: most people have no knowledge except of the world, its earnings, its affairs and what is in it. They are clever and astute in acquiring it and in the ways of gaining it, but they are heedless of what would benefit them in the Hereafter, as if one of them were a fool with no mind and no thought.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By Allah, the worldly concern of one of them reaches the point that he turns a dirham over on his fingernail and tells you its weight, yet he does not know how to pray properly."

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾: "It means the disbelievers. They know the prosperity of the world, but in matters of religion they are ignorant."

**Commentary on Surah al-Rum**

Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

These verses were revealed when Sabur (Shapur), king of the Persians, defeated the Romans in the lands of al-Sham (the Levant), in the districts of al-Jazirah adjoining it, and in the distant parts of the Roman lands. He forced Heraclius (Hiraql), king of the Romans, until he drove him to Constantinople (al-Qustantiniyyah) and besieged him there for a long time. Then the dynasty returned to Heraclius, as will come later.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr related to us, Abu Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land﴾. He said: "They were defeated and they defeated [others]." He said: "The polytheists (al-mushrikun) loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, because they were people of idols, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, they will be victorious.'" Abu Bakr mentioned that to them, and they said: "Set between us and you a term: if we prevail, we will have such-and-such, and if you prevail, you will have such-and-such." So he set a term of five years, but they did not prevail. Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Why did you not make it less than that?" I think he said: "Ten." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The bid' (a few) is less than ten." Then the Romans prevailed after that. He said: "That is His saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾."

This was related in the same way by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, both from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib (a good hadith with a single transmission route). We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan, from Habib."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir related it:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id, or Sa'id Abu Sa'd al-Tha'labi, who is called Abu Sa'd, from the people of Tarsus, related to us Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, and he mentioned it. In their version: Sufyan said: "It reached me that they were defeated on the day of Badr."

Another hadith: Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash related from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "Five have passed: the smoke (al-Dukhan), the inevitable punishment (al-Lizam), the great assault (al-Batshah), the moon (al-Qamar), and the Romans." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' related to us, al-Muharibi related to us, from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, that is al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Persia was dominant over the Romans, and the polytheists loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book and were closer to their religion. When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, they said: 'O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will prevail over Persia within a few years?!' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you bet with us on that?' So they made a wager with him for four she-camels up to seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened. The polytheists rejoiced at that, and it grieved the Muslims. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'What is a few years in your view?' They said: 'Less than ten.' He said: 'Go, increase the stakes for them and add two years to the term.' He said: 'The two years had not passed before riders came with news of the Romans' victory over Persia, and the believers rejoiced at that. Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ up to His saying: ﴿[the promise of Allah] Allah does not fail His promise﴾."

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Wakili related to us, Mu'ammal related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, the polytheists said to Abu Bakr: 'Do you not see what your companion says? He claims that the Romans will overcome Persia.' He said: 'My companion spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you like us to wager with you?' So he set a term between himself and them, but the term expired before the Romans overcame Persia. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and it displeased and disturbed him. He said to Abu Bakr: 'What prompted you to this?' He said: 'Confirmation of Allah and His Messenger.' He said: 'Go to them, increase the stake, and make the term a few years.' Abu Bakr came to them and said: 'Would you like to renew it, for renewal is better?' They said: 'Yes.' [He said:] The years had not passed before the Romans overcame Persia. They tied their horses in Madain (al-Mada'in), and they built al-Rumiyyah. Abu Bakr brought the winnings to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'This is unlawful gain.' He said: 'Give it in charity.'"

Another hadith: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Uways related to us, Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Nayyar ibn Mukram al-Aslami, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, Persia on the day this verse was revealed was dominating the Romans. The Muslims loved the victory of the Romans over them, because they and the Romans were People of the Book. Allah's saying concerning that is: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾. The Quraysh loved the victory of Persia, because they and the Persians were not People of the Book and did not believe in resurrection. When Allah revealed this verse, Abu Bakr went out crying in the outskirts of Makkah: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾. Some people of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: 'That is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will overcome Persia within a few years. Shall we wager you on that?' He said: 'Yes,' and that was before the prohibition of gambling. Abu Bakr and the polytheists placed stakes and agreed on the wager. They said to Abu Bakr: 'How many years do you set for the bid': three to nine years? Name a middle term between us and you, which we will reach.' He said: 'They set six years between them.' He said: 'The six years passed before they prevailed, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's pledge. When the seventh year arrived, the Romans prevailed over Persia.' The Muslims blamed Abu Bakr for naming six years. He said: 'Because Allah said: ﴿within a few years﴾.' He said: 'At that, many people embraced Islam.'"

This is how al-Tirmidhi related it, and then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith (good and authentic). We only know it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad. A similar report has been transmitted as mursal (with a gap in the chain), from a group of the Successors (tabi'un), such as 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Zuhri, and others."

Among the strangest of these accounts is what Imam Sunayd ibn Da'ud related in his tafsir, where he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "In Persia there was a woman who bore only kings and heroes. Kisra summoned her and said: 'I want to send an army to the Romans and appoint over them one of your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint.' She said: 'This one, so-and-so, is more cunning than a fox and more wary than a falcon. This one, Farkhan, is more penetrating than a spear. And this one, Shahriyaraz, is more forbearing than such-and-such,' meaning her three sons. 'Appoint whichever of them you wish.' He said: 'I have appointed the forbearing one.' So he appointed Shahriyaraz, who marched against the Romans with the people of Persia, prevailed over them, killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I related this hadith to 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and he said: 'Have you not seen the lands of al-Sham?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'If you had seen them, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down.' Then I went to al-Sham afterward and saw it." Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir from the route of Sunayd.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: Yahya ibn Ya'mar related to me that Caesar (Qaysar) sent a man called Qitmah with an army of Romans, and Kisra sent Shahriyaraz. They met at Adhru'at and Busra, which is the nearest part of al-Sham to you. Persia met the Romans and defeated them. The disbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims disliked it.

'Ikrimah said: "The polytheists met the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are unlettered. Our brothers from the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers from the People of the Book. If you fight us, we will surely prevail over you.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome. Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills﴾. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the disbelievers and said: 'Do you rejoice at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and may Allah not gladden your eyes. By Allah, Allah will surely give the Romans victory over Persia; our Prophet (ﷺ) told us of that.' Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up to him and said: 'You have lied, O Abu Fudayl.' Abu Bakr said to him: 'You are the greater liar, O enemy of Allah.' He said: 'I will wager you ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans prevail over Persia, I will pay, and if Persia prevails, you will pay, within three years.' Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'That is not how I mentioned it. The bid' is only what lies between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term.' Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy and said: 'Perhaps you regret it?' He said: 'No, come, I will increase the stake for you and extend the term. Make it a hundred she-camels for a hundred she-camels, up to nine years.' He said: 'I have done so.' Then the Romans prevailed over Persia before that time, and the Muslims were victorious."

Ikrimah said: When Persia prevailed over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and he was the brother of Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. He said to his companions: "I saw myself sitting on the throne of Kisra." This reached Kisra, and he wrote to Shahrayaz: "When my letter reaches you [[Addition from F.]], send me the head of Farkhan." Shahrayaz wrote back: "O King, you will not find another like Farkhan. He has force and a reputation among the enemy, so do not do this." Kisra wrote: "Among the men of Persia there are successors to him, so hasten to send me his head." Shahrayaz returned the matter to him, and Kisra became angry and did not answer him. He sent a courier to the people of Persia: "I have removed [[In F: "dismissed".]] Shahrayaz from you and appointed Farkhan over you." Then he gave the courier a small, delicate document and said: "When Farkhan takes power and his brother submits to him, give him this." When Shahrayaz read the letter, he said: "I hear and obey," and he got down from his throne, and Farkhan sat down, and Shahrayaz handed him the document. Farkhan said [[In F: "Then he said".]]: "Bring Shahrayaz to me," and had him brought forward to strike his neck. Shahrayaz said: "Do not hurry with me until I write my will." He said: "Yes." So he called for the chest, and Shahrayaz was given the pages [[In T, F, A: "three pages".]], and Farkhan said: "Kisra and I have gone back and forth over all this, and you wanted to kill me with a single letter." The king returned to his brother Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. Then Shahrayaz wrote to Qaysar, king of the Romans: "I have a need of you that neither the post-riders nor the pages can carry, so meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, and I will meet you with fifty Persians." Qaysar came with five hundred thousand Romans and placed spies before him along the road, fearing that he had been deceived, until his spies informed him that there were only fifty men with him. Then cushions were spread for the two of them, and they met in a brocade tent that had been pitched for them, each of them with a knife. They summoned an interpreter between them, and Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]] said: "Those who ruined your cities are I and my brother, through our cunning and our bravery. Kisra envied us, and he wanted me to kill my brother, but I refused, and then he ordered my brother to kill me. We have both deposed him, and so we are fighting him with you." He said: "You have done right." Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two, and if it passes two it spreads. He said: "Indeed." So they both killed the interpreter with their knives. Then God destroyed Kisra, and news of this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, and he rejoiced, and the Muslims rejoiced with him.

This is a strange narrative and a remarkable structure. Let us now discuss the words of these noble verses. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾, the discussion of the disjointed letters at the beginning of the surahs has already been given at the start of Surah al-Baqarah. As for the Romans (al-Rum), they are of the lineage of al-Is ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and they are cousins of the Children of Israel, and they are called the Sons of the Yellow (Banu al-Asfar). They followed the religion of the Greeks (al-Yunan), and the Greeks are of the lineage of Yafith ibn Nuh, paternal cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are called "the perplexed," and they prayed toward the North Pole. They are the ones who founded Damascus and built its temple, and in it there are prayer niches facing north. The Romans remained upon their religion until about three hundred years before the sending of the Messiah. The one who ruled Syria together with the Jazirah among them was called Qaysar. The first of the kings to enter the religion of the Christians was Constantine ibn Qastas, and his mother was Maryam al-Haylaniyyah al-Shadqaniyyah [[In T: "al-Qandaqaniyyah"; in F: "al-Ghandaqaniyyah".]] from the land of Harran. She had been a Christian before him, and she invited him to her religion. He had previously been a philosopher, so he followed her, it is said, out of dissimulation (taqiyyah). The Christians gathered around him, and in his time they debated with Abdullah ibn Aryus, and they differed in a widespread, scattered disagreement that could not be controlled. Yet three hundred and eighteen bishops from their assembly agreed, and they set down for Constantine the creed, which they call the Great Trust, though it is in fact the Base Betrayal. They also wrote for him the canons, meaning the books of rulings containing permitted and forbidden matters and other things they needed, and they altered the religion of the Messiah, peace be upon him, adding to it and subtracting from it. They went off toward the East, replaced the Sabbath with Sunday, worshipped the cross, and made the pig lawful. They instituted festivals that they invented, such as the feast of the Cross, the Qiddas, the Ghitas, and other innovations, the Bawa'ith and the Sha'anin, and they made the Pope their chief, then the Patriarchs, then the Metropolitans, then the Bishops and presbyters, then the deacons. They invented monasticism. The king built churches and temples for them, and he founded the city named after him, which is Constantinople. It is said that in his days he built twelve thousand churches, and he built Bethlehem with three prayer niches, and his mother built the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. These are the Melkites, meaning those who follow the religion of the king.

Then after them came the Jacobites, followers of Yaqub al-Iskaf, then the Nestorians, the companions of Nestora. They are many sects and groups, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They have split into seventy-two sects." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4596, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 3992. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "The chain of Awf ibn Malik has some criticism, and Rashid ibn Sa'd, Abu Hatim said of him: truthful. Abbad ibn Yusuf was narrated from only by Ibn Majah, and he has no other hadith in my view except this one; Ibn Adi said: he narrated hadiths that he alone transmitted. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and the rest of the men of the chain are trustworthy."]] The point is that they persisted in Christianity: whenever a Qaysar died, another succeeded him, until the last of them was Heraclius. He was one of the wisest of men, the most resolute and shrewd of kings, the deepest in insight and the most far-sighted in judgment. He ruled over them with great authority and great dignity. Kisra, king of the Persians, opposed him. Kisra ruled the lands such as Iraq, Khurasan, al-Rayy, and all the lands of the non-Arabs, and he was Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf. His kingdom was wider than the kingdom of Qaysar, and he had the leadership of the non-Arabs and the folly of the Persians. They were Magians who worshipped fire. It has been mentioned earlier from Ikrimah that he sent his deputies and his army to him, and they fought him. The well-known account is that Kisra himself invaded him in his lands, overpowered him, broke him, and humbled him, until nothing remained with him except the city of Constantinople. He besieged it for a long time until it grew tight for him. The Christians revered him exceedingly, and Kisra was unable to conquer the city, nor was it possible for him to do so because of its strength, since half of it lies on the land side and half on the sea side, and provisions and reinforcements kept reaching them from there. When the matter dragged on, Qaysar devised a stratagem and thought up a deception, so he asked Kisra to withdraw from his lands in exchange for money as a settlement, and he would stipulate whatever he wished. Kisra agreed to this and demanded from him enormous wealth, such as no king of the world could provide: gold, jewels, fabrics, slave girls, servants, and many kinds of goods. Qaysar complied and led him to believe that he had all that was requested. The pretense seemed small to him because of what was demanded, and had he and Kisra combined their power, they would have been unable to gather a tenth of it. He asked Kisra to allow him to go out to the lands of Syria and the regions of his kingdom to seek to collect this from his treasuries, storehouses, and hoards, and Kisra released him. When Qaysar resolved to leave Constantinople, he gathered the people of his religion and said: "I am going out on a matter I have settled, with a force I have chosen from my army. If I return to you before the year is out, I will be your king, and if I do not return to you before it, you have the choice: if you wish, continue in my allegiance, and if you wish, appoint someone other than me over you." They answered: "You are our king as long as you live, even if you are absent for ten years." When he left Constantinople, he set out lightly with a moderate army, while Kisra was camped around Constantinople waiting for him to return. Qaysar immediately mounted and marched swiftly until he reached the land of Persia, and he ravaged their lands, killing their men and the fighters among them, step by step, and he kept on killing until he reached al-Mada'in, which was the capital of Kisra's kingdom. He killed those in it, took all his stores and wealth, captured his women and harem, shaved the head of his son, mounted him on a donkey, and sent with him some of his own people, the Asawira, in utmost humiliation and abasement. He wrote to Kisra: "This is what you asked for, so take it." When this reached Kisra, grief overcame him to a degree that only God, Mighty and Majestic, can count, and his rage against the city intensified. He pressed hard in besieging it with every possible means, but he could not manage it. When he failed, he rode to block the road for him at the ford of the Jayhun, the only route by which Qaysar could reach Constantinople. When Qaysar learned of this, he devised a great stratagem unprecedented in its kind: he stationed his army and his stores with him at the mouth of the ford, rode out with part of the army, and ordered loads of straw, dung, and manure to be carried with him. He advanced upstream in the water for nearly a day, then ordered those loads to be thrown into the river. When they passed by Kisra, he and his army thought that they had crossed there, so they rode in pursuit of them, and the ford was left clear of the Persians. Qaysar came and ordered them to rise and enter the crossing, so they crossed and hurried their march, and they outpaced Kisra and his armies and entered Constantinople. That was a day remembered among the Christians, and Kisra and his armies remained bewildered, not knowing what to do. They had not gained the lands of Qaysar, while their own lands had been ravaged by the Romans, who had taken their stores and taken captive their offspring and women. So this was the Romans' victory over Persia, and it came nine years after the Persians' victory over the Romans.

The battle between Persia and the Romans, in which the Romans were defeated, took place between Adhruat and Busra, as reported by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. It is the frontier of the lands of Syria on the side adjoining the lands of the Hijaz.

Mujahid said: That happened in al-Jazirah, which is the nearest of the lands of the Romans to Persia. And God knows best.

Then the Romans defeated the Persians after a few years, and "a few years" means nine. In the Arabic language, *al-bidh'* (a few) refers to any number from three to nine. This is also what is related in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and others, through 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jumahi, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr during his pledge of allegiance [[In T: "mubayi'atihi" (his pledge of allegiance).]]: "Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated." (He said:) "Did you not take precaution, O Abu Bakr? Indeed, *al-bidh'* is between three and nine." Then he said: "This is a good, strange hadith from this route." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3191, and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/12).]]

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr that he said the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/16).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾, meaning: before that and after it. It is built on a *damm* (vowel) because the noun it modifies was cut off from the genitive construction, which is His saying *qabl* (before), with its implied complement intended.

﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah﴾, meaning: the Romans, the companions of Caesar, king of the Levant, over the Persians, the companions of Khosrow, who were Magians. The Roman victory over the Persians took place on the day of the Battle of Badr, according to a great number of scholars, such as Ibn 'Abbas, al-Thawri, al-Suddi and others. It has also been related in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bazzar, through al-A'mash, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When it was the day of Badr, the Romans prevailed over the Persians, and that pleased the believers and made them happy. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3192, and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/16).]]

Others said: Rather, the Roman victory over the Persians was in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. This was said by 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others. Some of them justified this view by saying that Caesar had vowed that if Allah granted him victory over Khosrow, he would walk from Homs to Iliya, which is Bayt al-Maqdis, in gratitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He did so. When he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, he did not leave it until there came to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he had sent with Dihya ibn Khalifa. Dihya gave it to the governor of Busra, and the governor of Busra delivered it to Caesar. When it reached him, he asked about the Arabs of Hijaz who were in the Levant. Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb al-Umawi was brought to him, along with a group of the Quraysh disbelievers who were in Gaza. They were brought to him and sat before him. He said: "Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?" Abu Sufyan said: "I am." He said to his companions, whom he had seated behind him: "I am going to ask this man about this man. If he lies, then contradict him." Abu Sufyan said: "By Allah, had it not been that they would have reported me as a liar, I would have lied." Heraclius asked him about his lineage and description. Among what he asked was: "Does he break his promises?" I said: "No. And we are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it," meaning the truce that had been concluded between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Quraysh disbelievers on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, to suspend hostilities between them for ten years. From this they inferred that the Roman victory over the Persians took place in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, because Caesar fulfilled his vow only after al-Hudaybiyah. And Allah knows best.

The proponents of the first view could respond to this by saying that his land had been ruined and disordered, so he was not able to fulfil his vow until he had restored what needed restoring and attended to his lands. Then, four years after his victory, he fulfilled his vow. And Allah knows best.

The matter in this is simple and near, except that when the Persians prevailed over the Romans, that grieved the believers, and when the Romans prevailed over the Persians, the believers rejoiced at that, because the Romans were in general a people of the Book, so they were closer to the believers than the Magians. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears from what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 82–83]. And Allah, the Exalted, said here: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Safwan related to us, al-Walid related to us, Usayd al-Kilabi related to me, who said: "I heard al-'Ala' ibn al-Zubayr al-Kilabi relate from his father, who said: 'I saw the Persians overcome the Romans, then I saw the Romans overcome the Persians, then I saw the Muslims overcome both the Persians and the Romans, all within fifteen years.'" [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim related from" (instead of "I heard").]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, meaning: in His victory and in His retribution against His enemies; ﴿the Merciful﴾, toward His believing servants.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah's promise. Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, meaning: this which We have informed you of, O Muhammad, that We will grant victory to the Romans over the Persians, is a promise from Allah that is true, and a true report that cannot be broken, and it must come to pass and occur. This is because Allah's custom is to grant victory to the nearer of the two fighting groups to the truth, and to make the final outcome theirs. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾, meaning: the wisdom of Allah in His creation and His actions, which are firm and proceed in accordance with justice.

* *

His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾, meaning: most people have no knowledge except of the world, its earnings, its affairs and what is in it. They are clever and astute in acquiring it and in the ways of gaining it, but they are heedless of what would benefit them in the Hereafter, as if one of them were a fool with no mind and no thought.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By Allah, the worldly concern of one of them reaches the point that he turns a dirham over on his fingernail and tells you its weight, yet he does not know how to pray properly."

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾: "It means the disbelievers. They know the prosperity of the world, but in matters of religion they are ignorant."

**Commentary on Surah al-Rum**

Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

These verses were revealed when Sabur (Shapur), king of the Persians, defeated the Romans in the lands of al-Sham (the Levant), in the districts of al-Jazirah adjoining it, and in the distant parts of the Roman lands. He forced Heraclius (Hiraql), king of the Romans, until he drove him to Constantinople (al-Qustantiniyyah) and besieged him there for a long time. Then the dynasty returned to Heraclius, as will come later.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr related to us, Abu Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land﴾. He said: "They were defeated and they defeated [others]." He said: "The polytheists (al-mushrikun) loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, because they were people of idols, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, they will be victorious.'" Abu Bakr mentioned that to them, and they said: "Set between us and you a term: if we prevail, we will have such-and-such, and if you prevail, you will have such-and-such." So he set a term of five years, but they did not prevail. Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Why did you not make it less than that?" I think he said: "Ten." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The bid' (a few) is less than ten." Then the Romans prevailed after that. He said: "That is His saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾."

This was related in the same way by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, both from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib (a good hadith with a single transmission route). We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan, from Habib."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir related it:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id, or Sa'id Abu Sa'd al-Tha'labi, who is called Abu Sa'd, from the people of Tarsus, related to us Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, and he mentioned it. In their version: Sufyan said: "It reached me that they were defeated on the day of Badr."

Another hadith: Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash related from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "Five have passed: the smoke (al-Dukhan), the inevitable punishment (al-Lizam), the great assault (al-Batshah), the moon (al-Qamar), and the Romans." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' related to us, al-Muharibi related to us, from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, that is al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Persia was dominant over the Romans, and the polytheists loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book and were closer to their religion. When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, they said: 'O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will prevail over Persia within a few years?!' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you bet with us on that?' So they made a wager with him for four she-camels up to seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened. The polytheists rejoiced at that, and it grieved the Muslims. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'What is a few years in your view?' They said: 'Less than ten.' He said: 'Go, increase the stakes for them and add two years to the term.' He said: 'The two years had not passed before riders came with news of the Romans' victory over Persia, and the believers rejoiced at that. Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ up to His saying: ﴿[the promise of Allah] Allah does not fail His promise﴾."

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Wakili related to us, Mu'ammal related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, the polytheists said to Abu Bakr: 'Do you not see what your companion says? He claims that the Romans will overcome Persia.' He said: 'My companion spoke the truth.' They said: 'Would you like us to wager with you?' So he set a term between himself and them, but the term expired before the Romans overcame Persia. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and it displeased and disturbed him. He said to Abu Bakr: 'What prompted you to this?' He said: 'Confirmation of Allah and His Messenger.' He said: 'Go to them, increase the stake, and make the term a few years.' Abu Bakr came to them and said: 'Would you like to renew it, for renewal is better?' They said: 'Yes.' [He said:] The years had not passed before the Romans overcame Persia. They tied their horses in Madain (al-Mada'in), and they built al-Rumiyyah. Abu Bakr brought the winnings to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'This is unlawful gain.' He said: 'Give it in charity.'"

Another hadith: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Uways related to us, Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Nayyar ibn Mukram al-Aslami, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾, Persia on the day this verse was revealed was dominating the Romans. The Muslims loved the victory of the Romans over them, because they and the Romans were People of the Book. Allah's saying concerning that is: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾. The Quraysh loved the victory of Persia, because they and the Persians were not People of the Book and did not believe in resurrection. When Allah revealed this verse, Abu Bakr went out crying in the outskirts of Makkah: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾. Some people of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: 'That is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will overcome Persia within a few years. Shall we wager you on that?' He said: 'Yes,' and that was before the prohibition of gambling. Abu Bakr and the polytheists placed stakes and agreed on the wager. They said to Abu Bakr: 'How many years do you set for the bid': three to nine years? Name a middle term between us and you, which we will reach.' He said: 'They set six years between them.' He said: 'The six years passed before they prevailed, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's pledge. When the seventh year arrived, the Romans prevailed over Persia.' The Muslims blamed Abu Bakr for naming six years. He said: 'Because Allah said: ﴿within a few years﴾.' He said: 'At that, many people embraced Islam.'"

This is how al-Tirmidhi related it, and then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith (good and authentic). We only know it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad. A similar report has been transmitted as mursal (with a gap in the chain), from a group of the Successors (tabi'un), such as 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Zuhri, and others."

Among the strangest of these accounts is what Imam Sunayd ibn Da'ud related in his tafsir, where he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "In Persia there was a woman who bore only kings and heroes. Kisra summoned her and said: 'I want to send an army to the Romans and appoint over them one of your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint.' She said: 'This one, so-and-so, is more cunning than a fox and more wary than a falcon. This one, Farkhan, is more penetrating than a spear. And this one, Shahriyaraz, is more forbearing than such-and-such,' meaning her three sons. 'Appoint whichever of them you wish.' He said: 'I have appointed the forbearing one.' So he appointed Shahriyaraz, who marched against the Romans with the people of Persia, prevailed over them, killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: "I related this hadith to 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and he said: 'Have you not seen the lands of al-Sham?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'If you had seen them, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down.' Then I went to al-Sham afterward and saw it." Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir from the route of Sunayd.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: Yahya ibn Ya'mar related to me that Caesar (Qaysar) sent a man called Qitmah with an army of Romans, and Kisra sent Shahriyaraz. They met at Adhru'at and Busra, which is the nearest part of al-Sham to you. Persia met the Romans and defeated them. The disbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims disliked it.

'Ikrimah said: "The polytheists met the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are unlettered. Our brothers from the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers from the People of the Book. If you fight us, we will surely prevail over you.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome. Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills﴾. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the disbelievers and said: 'Do you rejoice at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and may Allah not gladden your eyes. By Allah, Allah will surely give the Romans victory over Persia; our Prophet (ﷺ) told us of that.' Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up to him and said: 'You have lied, O Abu Fudayl.' Abu Bakr said to him: 'You are the greater liar, O enemy of Allah.' He said: 'I will wager you ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans prevail over Persia, I will pay, and if Persia prevails, you will pay, within three years.' Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'That is not how I mentioned it. The bid' is only what lies between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term.' Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy and said: 'Perhaps you regret it?' He said: 'No, come, I will increase the stake for you and extend the term. Make it a hundred she-camels for a hundred she-camels, up to nine years.' He said: 'I have done so.' Then the Romans prevailed over Persia before that time, and the Muslims were victorious."

Ikrimah said: When Persia prevailed over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and he was the brother of Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. He said to his companions: "I saw myself sitting on the throne of Kisra." This reached Kisra, and he wrote to Shahrayaz: "When my letter reaches you [[Addition from F.]], send me the head of Farkhan." Shahrayaz wrote back: "O King, you will not find another like Farkhan. He has force and a reputation among the enemy, so do not do this." Kisra wrote: "Among the men of Persia there are successors to him, so hasten to send me his head." Shahrayaz returned the matter to him, and Kisra became angry and did not answer him. He sent a courier to the people of Persia: "I have removed [[In F: "dismissed".]] Shahrayaz from you and appointed Farkhan over you." Then he gave the courier a small, delicate document and said: "When Farkhan takes power and his brother submits to him, give him this." When Shahrayaz read the letter, he said: "I hear and obey," and he got down from his throne, and Farkhan sat down, and Shahrayaz handed him the document. Farkhan said [[In F: "Then he said".]]: "Bring Shahrayaz to me," and had him brought forward to strike his neck. Shahrayaz said: "Do not hurry with me until I write my will." He said: "Yes." So he called for the chest, and Shahrayaz was given the pages [[In T, F, A: "three pages".]], and Farkhan said: "Kisra and I have gone back and forth over all this, and you wanted to kill me with a single letter." The king returned to his brother Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]]. Then Shahrayaz wrote to Qaysar, king of the Romans: "I have a need of you that neither the post-riders nor the pages can carry, so meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, and I will meet you with fifty Persians." Qaysar came with five hundred thousand Romans and placed spies before him along the road, fearing that he had been deceived, until his spies informed him that there were only fifty men with him. Then cushions were spread for the two of them, and they met in a brocade tent that had been pitched for them, each of them with a knife. They summoned an interpreter between them, and Shahrayaz [[In T: "Shahrizar".]] said: "Those who ruined your cities are I and my brother, through our cunning and our bravery. Kisra envied us, and he wanted me to kill my brother, but I refused, and then he ordered my brother to kill me. We have both deposed him, and so we are fighting him with you." He said: "You have done right." Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two, and if it passes two it spreads. He said: "Indeed." So they both killed the interpreter with their knives. Then God destroyed Kisra, and news of this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, and he rejoiced, and the Muslims rejoiced with him.

This is a strange narrative and a remarkable structure. Let us now discuss the words of these noble verses. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾, the discussion of the disjointed letters at the beginning of the surahs has already been given at the start of Surah al-Baqarah. As for the Romans (al-Rum), they are of the lineage of al-Is ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and they are cousins of the Children of Israel, and they are called the Sons of the Yellow (Banu al-Asfar). They followed the religion of the Greeks (al-Yunan), and the Greeks are of the lineage of Yafith ibn Nuh, paternal cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are called "the perplexed," and they prayed toward the North Pole. They are the ones who founded Damascus and built its temple, and in it there are prayer niches facing north. The Romans remained upon their religion until about three hundred years before the sending of the Messiah. The one who ruled Syria together with the Jazirah among them was called Qaysar. The first of the kings to enter the religion of the Christians was Constantine ibn Qastas, and his mother was Maryam al-Haylaniyyah al-Shadqaniyyah [[In T: "al-Qandaqaniyyah"; in F: "al-Ghandaqaniyyah".]] from the land of Harran. She had been a Christian before him, and she invited him to her religion. He had previously been a philosopher, so he followed her, it is said, out of dissimulation (taqiyyah). The Christians gathered around him, and in his time they debated with Abdullah ibn Aryus, and they differed in a widespread, scattered disagreement that could not be controlled. Yet three hundred and eighteen bishops from their assembly agreed, and they set down for Constantine the creed, which they call the Great Trust, though it is in fact the Base Betrayal. They also wrote for him the canons, meaning the books of rulings containing permitted and forbidden matters and other things they needed, and they altered the religion of the Messiah, peace be upon him, adding to it and subtracting from it. They went off toward the East, replaced the Sabbath with Sunday, worshipped the cross, and made the pig lawful. They instituted festivals that they invented, such as the feast of the Cross, the Qiddas, the Ghitas, and other innovations, the Bawa'ith and the Sha'anin, and they made the Pope their chief, then the Patriarchs, then the Metropolitans, then the Bishops and presbyters, then the deacons. They invented monasticism. The king built churches and temples for them, and he founded the city named after him, which is Constantinople. It is said that in his days he built twelve thousand churches, and he built Bethlehem with three prayer niches, and his mother built the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. These are the Melkites, meaning those who follow the religion of the king.

Then after them came the Jacobites, followers of Yaqub al-Iskaf, then the Nestorians, the companions of Nestora. They are many sects and groups, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They have split into seventy-two sects." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4596, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 3992. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "The chain of Awf ibn Malik has some criticism, and Rashid ibn Sa'd, Abu Hatim said of him: truthful. Abbad ibn Yusuf was narrated from only by Ibn Majah, and he has no other hadith in my view except this one; Ibn Adi said: he narrated hadiths that he alone transmitted. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and the rest of the men of the chain are trustworthy."]] The point is that they persisted in Christianity: whenever a Qaysar died, another succeeded him, until the last of them was Heraclius. He was one of the wisest of men, the most resolute and shrewd of kings, the deepest in insight and the most far-sighted in judgment. He ruled over them with great authority and great dignity. Kisra, king of the Persians, opposed him. Kisra ruled the lands such as Iraq, Khurasan, al-Rayy, and all the lands of the non-Arabs, and he was Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf. His kingdom was wider than the kingdom of Qaysar, and he had the leadership of the non-Arabs and the folly of the Persians. They were Magians who worshipped fire. It has been mentioned earlier from Ikrimah that he sent his deputies and his army to him, and they fought him. The well-known account is that Kisra himself invaded him in his lands, overpowered him, broke him, and humbled him, until nothing remained with him except the city of Constantinople. He besieged it for a long time until it grew tight for him. The Christians revered him exceedingly, and Kisra was unable to conquer the city, nor was it possible for him to do so because of its strength, since half of it lies on the land side and half on the sea side, and provisions and reinforcements kept reaching them from there.
