**Ibn Kathir's Tafsir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim), on Surah 30, verses 30–32:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾. That is, persist in what Allah has prescribed for you, of the *hanifiyyah* (the pure monotheistic disposition), the *millat Ibrahim* (the creed of Ibrahim), which Allah guided you to and perfected for you to the utmost perfection. And you, along with that, must adhere to your sound *fitrah* (innate nature), upon which Allah created creation. For He, the Exalted, created His creatures upon [knowledge of Him and His oneness, and that there is no god besides Him, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam... Am I not your Lord? They said, "Yes"﴾ (Al-A'raf: 172). And in a hadith: "Indeed I created My servants as *hunafa'* (upright monotheists), but the devils turned them away from their religion." We will mention in the hadiths that Allah the Exalted created His creatures upon] [Islam (this addition is from manuscripts T and A)]. Then false religions afflicted some of them, such as Judaism, Christianity or Zoroastrianism. [In manuscripts T and F: "and Christianity and Zoroastrianism."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is, "Do not alter the creation of Allah," so that you do not change people from their *fitrah* upon which Allah created them. Thus it is a report with the meaning of a command, like His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it shall be safe﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 97). This is a good and sound meaning.

Others said: it is a report on its own basis, and its meaning is that Allah made all His creatures equal in the *fitrah*, upon the upright natural disposition. No one is born except upon that, and there is no difference among people in that. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd [in manuscript T: "and Sa'id ibn Hubayr and others"] said regarding His saying ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾: that is, the religion of Allah.

Al-Bukhari said: His saying ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾: "[It means] the religion of Allah; the creation of the former ones: [the religion of the former ones]; and the religion and the *fitrah* is Islam."

'Abdan narrated to us: 'Abdullah informed us: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except upon the *fitrah*, and then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see in it any mutilation?" Then he recites: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no change in the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30].

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, from al-Zuhri, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4775; Sahih Muslim no. 2658]. Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6599; Sahih Muslim no. 2658].

Regarding the meaning of this hadith, hadiths have been narrated from a group of the Companions. Among them is al-Aswad ibn Sari' al-Tamimi. Imam Ahmad said:

Isma'il narrated to us: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' [al-Tamimi] [addition from manuscript F], who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I fought with him, and I obtained spoils [in manuscripts T and F: "victory"], and the people killed that day, until they killed the children. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "What is the matter with people who have gone beyond killing today, until they have killed the offspring?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not the children of the polytheists?" He said: "Indeed, the best of you are the children of the polytheists." Then he said: "Do not kill offspring, do not kill offspring." And he said: "Every soul is born upon the *fitrah* until its tongue expresses itself, and then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian."

An-Nasa'i narrated it in *Kitab al-Siyar*, from Ziyad ibn Ayyub, from Hushaym, from Yunus, who is Ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, with the same chain [in manuscript T: "and he narrated also with his chain"] [Musnad 3/435; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 8616].

Among them is Jabir ibn 'Abdullah al-Ansari. Imam Ahmad said:

Hashim narrated to us: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from al-Hasan, from Jabir, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the *fitrah* until its tongue expresses itself; then when its tongue expresses itself, either it is grateful or it is ungrateful" [Musnad 3/353; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/218): "In it is Abu Ja'far al-Razi, who is trustworthy though there is some disagreement about him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."].

Among them is 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas al-Hashimi. Imam Ahmad said:

'Affan narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr [in manuscript T: "and he narrated also with his chain"], from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "Allah knows best what they would have done had they lived." [Musnad 1/328; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1383; Sahih Muslim no. 2660.] Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it in their *Sahihs*, from the hadith of Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Iyas al-Yashkuri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a marfu' (directly attributed to the Prophet) report of this.

Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad, that is Ibn Salamah, narrated to us: 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar informed us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: There came upon me a time when I used to say: "The children of the Muslims are with the children of the Muslims, and the children of the polytheists are with the polytheists," until so-and-so narrated to me, from so-and-so [in manuscripts T and F: "from Ibn so-and-so"], that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about them, and he said: "Allah knows best what they would have done." He said: "I met the man and he informed me, so I held back from my statement" [Musnad 5/73; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/218): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."].

Among them is 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i. Imam Ahmad said:

Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Iyad ibn Himar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon one day, and in his sermon he said: "Indeed my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me to teach you what you do not know, of what He taught me on this day: every wealth that I have granted to My servants is lawful. Indeed I created My servants as *hunafa'*, all of them, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, looked at the people of the earth and despised them, Arabs and non-Arabs, except for remnants of the People of the Book. And He said: 'I have only sent you to test you and to test others through you, and I have sent down to you a Book which water cannot wash away; you recite it while sleeping and awake.'

"Then Allah commanded me to burn Quraysh. I said: 'O Lord, then they will crush my head so that it becomes like a crushed loaf.' He said: 'Expel them as they expelled you, fight them and We shall support you, spend upon them and We shall spend upon you, send an army and We shall send five times its like, and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you.'"

He said: "The people of Paradise are three: a ruler who is just, charitable and guided; a man who is merciful and tender-hearted toward every relative and every Muslim; and a chaste, poor man who gives charity. The people of the Fire are five: the weak one who has no judgment, who follows you without seeking family or wealth; the traitor, who does not conceal any greed, however small, without betraying it; and a man who does not rise in the morning or evening except that he deceives you regarding your family and your wealth." And he mentioned the miser or the liar, and *al-Shanzir* is the vulgar, foul-mouthed person.

Muslim alone narrated it, transmitting it through several chains from Qatadah, with the same [Musnad 4/162; Sahih Muslim no. 2865].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾. That is: adherence to the Law and the sound *fitrah* is the straight, correct religion. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾. That is: for this reason most people do not recognize it, and they turn away from it, as He said: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive, are not believers﴾ (Yusuf: 103), and ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ (Al-An'am: 116), and the verse continues.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Turning back to Him in repentance﴾. Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about people that in a state of distress they call upon Allah alone, with no partner, and that when He bestows blessings upon them, a group of them [that is, [in a state of] testing] [Addition from manuscript A.] associate others with Allah and worship others alongside Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿so that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of consequence (*lam al-'aqibah*) according to some scholars, and the lam of causation (*lam al-ta'lil*) according to others. However, it is a causation for Allah's enabling them to do this [Addition from manuscript A.].

Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿So you will come to know﴾ [In manuscript T: "they will know".] Some of them said: "By Allah, if a guard of a street threatened me, I would fear him. Ibn Kathir said, commenting on verse 38 onward:

Allah, exalted is He, commands the giving of what is due to the kinsman (dhi al-qurba) of his right, meaning through kindness and maintaining ties, and to the needy (al-miskin), who is the one who has nothing to spend on him or has something that does not suffice for his needs, and to the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), who is the traveler in need of provision and what he requires on his journey. "That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah," meaning the looking upon Him on the Day of Resurrection, which is the ultimate goal. "And those are the successful," meaning in this world and in the Hereafter.

Then He said: "And whatever you give in interest (riba) to increase the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah." Meaning: whoever gives a gift, desiring that people return more than what he gave them, for such a person there is no reward with Allah. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Sha'bi explained it in this way. This practice is permissible, although there is no reward in it, except that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) specifically forbade it, as al-Dahhak said, and he cited as evidence His saying: "And do not give, seeking to receive more" (al-Muddaththir: 6), meaning: do not give a gift desiring more than it.

Ibn Abbas said: Riba is of two kinds: one riba that is not valid, meaning riba of trade (al-bay'), and one riba that is not blameworthy, which is a man's gift that he intends to receive its equal or multiples. Then he recited this verse: "And whatever you give in interest to increase the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah."

The reward with Allah is only in zakat. Therefore He said: "And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the Face of Allah, those are the multipliers," meaning those whom Allah multiplies the reward and recompense for. As is in the Sahih: "No one gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, except that the Most Merciful takes it with His right hand, and nurtures it for its giver just as one of you raises his foal or young camel, until the date becomes greater than Uhud." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1410.)

* *

His saying: "Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you" means: He is the Creator, the Provider. He brings forth man from his mother's womb naked, without knowledge, hearing, sight or faculties, then He provides him with all of that afterward, and with fine clothing, garments, wealth, possessions and means of earning, as Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sallam Abu Shurahbil, from Habbah and Sawa' the two sons of Khalid, who said: We entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was repairing something, so we helped him. He said: "Do not despair of provision as long as your heads move; for indeed man is born by his mother red, with no covering on him, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provides for him." (Musnad, 3/469.)

* *

His saying: "Then He causes you to die," meaning after this life, "then He gives you life," meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

His saying: "Is there any of your partners who does any of that?" meaning those you worship besides Allah. "None of them is able to do anything of that," meaning none of them can do any of that. Rather Allah, glorified and exalted, alone is the One who independently creates, provides, gives life and causes death, and then He resurrects all creation on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore He said after all of this: "Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him," meaning He is exalted, sanctified, purified, magnified, majestic and mighty above having any partner, equal or peer, or son or father. Rather He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.

Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and others said: By "the land" (al-barr) here is meant the deserts (al-fayafi), and by "the sea" (al-bahr) are meant the cities and villages. In another narration from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿIkrimah: "the sea" means the cities and villages that lie on the bank of a river.

Others said: rather, by "the land" is meant the well-known land, and by "the sea" the well-known sea.

Zayd ibn Rufayʿ said concerning ﴿Corruption has appeared﴾: it means the cessation of rain from the land, which is followed by drought, and from the sea, its creatures die. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

He also said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd ibn Qays al-Aʿraj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾: he said, "The corruption of the land is the killing of the son of Adam, and the corruption of the sea is seizing ships by force."

ʿAta al-Khurasani said: By "the land" is meant what it contains of cities and villages, and by "the sea" its islands.

The first opinion is the most apparent, and most scholars hold it. It is supported by what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with the king of Aylah, and wrote to him concerning his sea, meaning his land.

As for the meaning of His statement, ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾: that is, the shortfall in fruits and crops became evident because of sins.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: Whoever disobeys Allah on the earth has corrupted the earth, because the goodness of the earth and the heavens is through obedience. For this reason a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud states: "A prescribed punishment (hadd) carried out on earth is dearer to its people than being given rain for forty mornings." [Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (2/362) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (8/75) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah; it did not come to me in the Sunan of Abu Dawud.] The reason for this is that when the prescribed punishments are enforced, people (or most of them, or many of them) refrain from engaging in what is forbidden; and when sins are committed, they become a cause for the loss of blessings from the heavens and the earth. For this reason, when ʿIsa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) descends at the end of time and judges by this purified law at that time—killing the swine, breaking the cross, and abolishing the jizyah (that is, not accepting it), accepting nothing but Islam or the sword—then when Allah destroys in his time the Dajjal and his followers and Yajuj and Majuj, it will be said to the earth: "Bring forth your blessings." A group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and shelter under its peel, and the milk of one she-camel will suffice a whole company of people. This is only by the blessing of implementing the Shari'ah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); whenever justice is established, blessings and good abound. [For this reason] it is established in the Sahih: "When a wicked person dies, the servants, the lands, the trees and the animals find relief from him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6512).]

For this reason Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Muhammad and al-Husayn narrated to us, both saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Abu Qahdham, who said: A man in the time of Ziyad—or Ibn Ziyad—found a purse containing grain, meaning wheat, like date pits, on which was written: "This grew in a time when justice was practised." [al-Musnad (2/296).]

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam that the corruption meant here is shirk. But there is consideration in this.

As for His statement, ﴿That He may let them taste some of what they have done, so that they may return﴾: that is, He tests them with the loss of wealth, lives and fruits, as a trial from Him and as a recompense for their deeds, ﴿so that they may return﴾: that is, from sins, as He said, ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad, so that they might return﴾ [al-A'raf: 168].

Then He said, ﴿Say: Travel in the earth and see how was the end of those before [you]﴾: that is, before you, ﴿most of them were polytheists﴾: that is, look at what befell them from denying the messengers and disbelieving the blessings.

Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and others said: By "the land" (al-barr) here is meant the deserts (al-fayafi), and by "the sea" (al-bahr) are meant the cities and villages. In another narration from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿIkrimah: "the sea" means the cities and villages that lie on the bank of a river.

Others said: rather, by "the land" is meant the well-known land, and by "the sea" the well-known sea.

Zayd ibn Rufayʿ said concerning ﴿Corruption has appeared﴾: it means the cessation of rain from the land, which is followed by drought, and from the sea, its creatures die. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

He also said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd ibn Qays al-Aʿraj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾: he said, "The corruption of the land is the killing of the son of Adam, and the corruption of the sea is seizing ships by force."

ʿAta al-Khurasani said: By "the land" is meant what it contains of cities and villages, and by "the sea" its islands.

The first opinion is the most apparent, and most scholars hold it. It is supported by what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with the king of Aylah, and wrote to him concerning his sea, meaning his land.

As for the meaning of His statement, ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾: that is, the shortfall in fruits and crops became evident because of sins.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: Whoever disobeys Allah on the earth has corrupted the earth, because the goodness of the earth and the heavens is through obedience. For this reason a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud states: "A prescribed punishment (hadd) carried out on earth is dearer to its people than being given rain for forty mornings." [Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (2/362) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (8/75) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah; it did not come to me in the Sunan of Abu Dawud.] The reason for this is that when the prescribed punishments are enforced, people (or most of them, or many of them) refrain from engaging in what is forbidden; and when sins are committed, they become a cause for the loss of blessings from the heavens and the earth. For this reason, when ʿIsa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) descends at the end of time and judges by this purified law at that time—killing the swine, breaking the cross, and abolishing the jizyah (that is, not accepting it), accepting nothing but Islam or the sword—then when Allah destroys in his time the Dajjal and his followers and Yajuj and Majuj, it will be said to the earth: "Bring forth your blessings." A group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and shelter under its peel, and the milk of one she-camel will suffice a whole company of people. This is only by the blessing of implementing the Shari'ah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); whenever justice is established, blessings and good abound. [For this reason] it is established in the Sahih: "When a wicked person dies, the servants, the lands, the trees and the animals find relief from him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6512).]

For this reason Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Muhammad and al-Husayn narrated to us, both saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Abu Qahdham, who said: A man in the time of Ziyad—or Ibn Ziyad—found a purse containing grain, meaning wheat, like date pits, on which was written: "This grew in a time when justice was practised." [al-Musnad (2/296).]

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His servants to hasten to steadfastness in obedience to Him and to hasten to good deeds: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion before there comes from Allah a Day which no one can avert.﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection, which, when Allah wills it to occur, none can turn back. ﴿On that Day they will be divided.﴾ That is, they will separate: a group will be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze (al-Sa'ir). Hence He said: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteousness - for themselves they are preparing [a resting place],﴾ ﴿that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds from His bounty.﴾ That is, He will recompense them with the recompense of bounty: a good deed with ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and beyond that to whatever Allah wills. ﴿Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.﴾ And despite this, He is the Just regarding them, who does not oppress.

He, may He be exalted, mentions His blessings upon His creation in sending the winds as bearers of good tidings before His mercy, with the rain and the abundance coming after them. So He said: ﴿And that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, meaning the rain which He sends down, by which He gives life to the servants and the lands. ﴿And that the ships may run by His command﴾, meaning on the sea, and it is the wind that makes them move. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning through trade and livelihoods, and travel from one region to another and from one land to another. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning that you will thank Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, both the outward and the inward, which cannot be counted or enumerated.

Then He said: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, then We took vengeance upon those who committed crime. And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers.﴾ This is a consolation from Allah to His servant and messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that although many of his people and of mankind denied him, the messengers before him were also denied, even though they brought their nations clear signs. But Allah took vengeance upon those who denied and opposed them, and He saved the believers who followed them. ﴿And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾: it is a right that He made obligatory upon Himself, out of His generosity and bounty, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 54].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Musa ibn A'yan narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no Muslim man who defends the honour of his brother, except that it is a right upon Allah to protect him from the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾.

Ibn Kathir explains how God creates the clouds from which water descends. He says: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, either from the sea, as several scholars have mentioned, or from whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills. ﴿Then He spreads them across the sky however He wills﴾, meaning He extends them, makes them abundant and increases them, and turns little into much. He brings forth a cloud which, to the eye, looks like a shield, then spreads it until it fills the expanses of the horizon. Sometimes the cloud comes from the direction of the sea, heavy and full of water, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water therewith, and bring forth thereby fruits of all kinds. Thus do We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember﴾ [al-A'raf: 57]. Likewise He says here: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, then He spreads them across the sky however He wills and makes them fragments﴾. Mujahid, Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', Matar al-Warraq and Qatadah said: this means pieces. Someone else said: piled up, as reported from al-Dahhak. Yet another said: black from the abundance of water, appearing dark, heavy and close to the earth.

And His saying ﴿you see the rain coming out from between them﴾ means: you see the rain, which is the drops, emerging from between those clouds. ﴿Then when He causes it to strike whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾ means: because of their need for it, they rejoice at its descent upon them and its reaching them.

And His saying: ﴿And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, certainly in despair﴾. The meaning of the statement is that these people upon whom this rain fell had been despairing and hopeless of the rain reaching them before that. When it came to them, it came upon them in their dire need, and it had a tremendous effect upon them.

The grammarians differed concerning His saying: ﴿before it was sent down upon them, certainly in despair﴾. Ibn Jarir said: it is an emphasis (ta'kid), and he related this from some of the people of Arabic. Others said: "[And even though they were] before the rain was sent down upon them, ﴿before it﴾, i.e., before the sending down, ﴿certainly in despair﴾."

It may be that this is of the type of "ta'sis" (establishing new meaning), and the meaning of the statement would be: they were in need of it before its descent, and also before it, its descent had been delayed for them time after time, so they awaited it at its proper season, but it was late; a period passed and they awaited it, but it was late; then it came to them suddenly after they had despaired of it and lost hope. So after their land had been parched and lifeless, it became stirred and swelling, and sprouted every lovely pair. Therefore He says: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, meaning the rain.

Then through this He drew attention to the revival of bodies after their death, dispersal and disintegration, saying: ﴿Indeed, that is the One who will surely bring the dead to life﴾, i.e., indeed He who did that is capable of bringing the dead to life, ﴿indeed He is over all things competent﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow, they would surely remain afterward in disbelief﴾. He says: ﴿And if We sent a wind﴾, dry, upon the crop they had sown, which had grown, flourished and stood on its stalk, and they saw it turned yellow, i.e., it had yellowed and begun to decay, ﴿they would remain afterward﴾, i.e., after this condition, ﴿in disbelief﴾, i.e., they would deny the blessings that had previously come to them, as He says: ﴿Have you considered what you plant? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers? If We willed, We would make it into debris, and you would remain astonished, [saying], "Indeed, we are burdened with debt. Rather, we have been deprived"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63–67].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba' related to us, Hushaim related to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The winds are eight: four of them are mercy and four are punishment. As for the mercy: the ones that spread (al-nashirat), the ones that bring good tidings (al-mubashshirat), the ones that are sent (al-mursalat), and the ones that scatter (al-dhariyat). As for the punishment: the barren (al-'aqim) and the violent cold (al-sarsar), which are on land, and the strong (al-'asif) and the crushing (al-qasif), which are at sea. [When He, glory be to Him and exalted, wills, He moves it with the movement of mercy and makes it gentle, mercy, and good tidings before His mercy, and a fertilizing agent for the clouds, fertilizing them by carrying water, as a male fertilizes a female by impregnation; and if He wills, He moves it with the movement of punishment and makes it barren, and deposits in it painful torment, and makes it a vengeance upon whomever He wills of His servants, so He makes it violent, transgressing, and corrupting whatever passes over it. Winds differ in their directions: the east wind, the west wind, the south wind, and the north wind, and in their benefit and effect there is the greatest difference: a wind that is soft and moist which nourishes plants and the bodies of animals, another that dries them, another that destroys and ruins them, another that moves and hardens them, and another that weakens and enfeebles them.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu 'Ubayd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, related to us; my uncle related to us; 'Abdullah ibn 'Ayyash related to us; 'Abdullah ibn Sulayman related to me, from Darraj, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wind is subjected from the second [earth], meaning the second earth. When Allah wished to destroy 'Ad, He commanded the keeper of the wind to send upon them a wind that would destroy 'Ad. He said: 'O Lord, shall I send upon them wind the size of an ox's nostril?' The Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, said to him: 'No, for then it would overturn the earth and whatever is on it. Rather, send upon them an amount the size of a ring.'" This is the one of which Allah said in His Book: ﴿It leaves nothing it passes over but makes it like ruin﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 42]. This is a strange hadith, and its marfu' form is munkar. The more apparent view is that it is a statement of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.

He says: ﴿And if We sent a wind﴾, dry, upon the crop they had sown, which had grown, flourished and stood on its stalk, and they saw it turned yellow, i.e., it had yellowed and begun to decay, ﴿they would remain afterward﴾, i.e., after this condition, ﴿in disbelief﴾, i.e., they would deny the blessings that had previously come to them, as He says: ﴿Have you considered what you plant? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers? If We willed, We would make it into debris, and you would remain astonished, [saying], "Indeed, we are burdened with debt. Rather, we have been deprived"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63–67].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba' related to us, Hushaim related to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The winds are eight: four of them are mercy and four are punishment. As for the mercy: the ones that spread (al-nashirat), the ones that bring good tidings (al-mubashshirat), the ones that are sent (al-mursalat), and the ones that scatter (al-dhariyat). As for the punishment: the barren (al-'aqim) and the violent cold (al-sarsar), which are on land, and the strong (al-'asif) and the crushing (al-qasif), which are at sea. [When He, glory be to Him and exalted, wills, He moves it with the movement of mercy and makes it gentle, mercy, and good tidings before His mercy, and a fertilizing agent for the clouds, fertilizing them by carrying water, as a male fertilizes a female by impregnation; and if He wills, He moves it with the movement of punishment and makes it barren, and deposits in it painful torment, and makes it a vengeance upon whomever He wills of His servants, so He makes it violent, transgressing, and corrupting whatever passes over it. Winds differ in their directions: the east wind, the west wind, the south wind, and the north wind, and in their benefit and effect there is the greatest difference: a wind that is soft and moist which nourishes plants and the bodies of animals, another that dries them, another that destroys and ruins them, another that moves and hardens them, and another that weakens and enfeebles them.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu 'Ubayd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, related to us; my uncle related to us; 'Abdullah ibn 'Ayyash related to us; 'Abdullah ibn Sulayman related to me, from Darraj, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wind is subjected from the second [earth], meaning the second earth. When Allah wished to destroy 'Ad, He commanded the keeper of the wind to send upon them a wind that would destroy 'Ad. He said: 'O Lord, shall I send upon them wind the size of an ox's nostril?' The Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, said to him: 'No, for then it would overturn the earth and whatever is on it. Rather, send upon them an amount the size of a ring.'" This is the one of which Allah said in His Book: ﴿It leaves nothing it passes over but makes it like ruin﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 42]. This is a strange hadith, and its marfu' form is munkar. The more apparent view is that it is a statement of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.

Ibn Kathir explains how God creates the clouds from which water descends. He says: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, either from the sea, as several scholars have mentioned, or from whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills. ﴿Then He spreads them across the sky however He wills﴾, meaning He extends them, makes them abundant and increases them, and turns little into much. He brings forth a cloud which, to the eye, looks like a shield, then spreads it until it fills the expanses of the horizon. Sometimes the cloud comes from the direction of the sea, heavy and full of water, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water therewith, and bring forth thereby fruits of all kinds. Thus do We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember﴾ [al-A'raf: 57]. Likewise He says here: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, then He spreads them across the sky however He wills and makes them fragments﴾. Mujahid, Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', Matar al-Warraq and Qatadah said: this means pieces. Someone else said: piled up, as reported from al-Dahhak. Yet another said: black from the abundance of water, appearing dark, heavy and close to the earth.

And His saying ﴿you see the rain coming out from between them﴾ means: you see the rain, which is the drops, emerging from between those clouds. ﴿Then when He causes it to strike whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾ means: because of their need for it, they rejoice at its descent upon them and its reaching them.

And His saying: ﴿And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, certainly in despair﴾. The meaning of the statement is that these people upon whom this rain fell had been despairing and hopeless of the rain reaching them before that. When it came to them, it came upon them in their dire need, and it had a tremendous effect upon them.

The grammarians differed concerning His saying: ﴿before it was sent down upon them, certainly in despair﴾. Ibn Jarir said: it is an emphasis (ta'kid), and he related this from some of the people of Arabic. Others said: "[And even though they were] before the rain was sent down upon them, ﴿before it﴾, i.e., before the sending down, ﴿certainly in despair﴾."

It may be that this is of the type of "ta'sis" (establishing new meaning), and the meaning of the statement would be: they were in need of it before its descent, and also before it, its descent had been delayed for them time after time, so they awaited it at its proper season, but it was late; a period passed and they awaited it, but it was late; then it came to them suddenly after they had despaired of it and lost hope. So after their land had been parched and lifeless, it became stirred and swelling, and sprouted every lovely pair. Therefore He says: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, meaning the rain.

Then through this He drew attention to the revival of bodies after their death, dispersal and disintegration, saying: ﴿Indeed, that is the One who will surely bring the dead to life﴾, i.e., indeed He who did that is capable of bringing the dead to life, ﴿indeed He is over all things competent﴾.

The Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, said to him: 'No, for then it would overturn the earth and whatever is on it. Rather, send upon them an amount the size of a ring.'" God, Exalted is He, says: Just as you have no power to make the dead in their graves hear, and you cannot make the deaf who do not hear hear your words, even though they turn away from you, so too you cannot guide the blind away from the truth and turn them back from their misguidance. Rather, that is up to God, Exalted is He. By His power He makes the dead hear the voices of the living whenever He wills, He guides whom He wills, and He leads astray whom He wills, and this belongs to no one but Him. Therefore He said: ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, and they are submitting﴾, meaning: humbling themselves, responding, and obeying. These are the ones who listen to the truth and follow it, and this is the condition of the believers. The first (the deaf and the dead) is the condition of the disbelievers, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Only those who listen will respond. As for the dead, God will raise them, then to Him they will be returned﴾ [al-An'am: 36].

Umm al-Mu'minin 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, cited this verse, ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾, to cast doubt on the report of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar that the Prophet ﷺ addressed the slain who had been thrown into the well of Badr, three days later, and rebuked and reproached them. 'Umar said to him: "O Messenger of God, why do you address people who have already rotted?" He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear what I say than they are, but they cannot respond." 'Aisha interpreted it as meaning that he said: "Now they know that what I used to tell them was true."

[Al-Zarkashi, may God have mercy on him, in his book "al-Ijaba li-Iraad ma Istadrakathu 'Aisha 'ala al-Sahaba" (p. 121), said: "al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Umar that he said: The Prophet ﷺ stopped at the well of Badr and said: 'Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' Then he said: 'Indeed, they now hear what I say.' This was mentioned to 'Aisha, and she said: The Prophet ﷺ only said: 'Indeed, they now know that what I used to tell them is true.'" Al-Suhayli said in al-Rawd: "'Aisha was not present, while others who were present are more reliable in preserving his exact words ﷺ. They said to him: 'O Messenger of God, do you address a people who have rotted, or who have decayed?' He said: 'You are no more able to hear what I say than they are.' If it is possible for them in that state to know, it is possible for them to hear, either with the ears of their heads, if we say that the spirit is returned to the body or to part of it at the time of questioning, which is the view of the majority of the People of the Sunnah, or with the ear of the heart or the spirit, according to the view of those who say that the questioning is directed to the spirit without the return to the body or to part of it." He said: "It has been related that 'Aisha argued from His saying: ﴿And you cannot make those in the graves hear﴾ [Fatir: 22]. This verse is like His saying: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind?﴾ meaning: it is God who guides, grants success, and brings admonition into the ears of hearts, not you. He described the disbelievers as dead and deaf by way of comparison with the dead and the deaf. God is the one who truly makes them hear whenever He wills. So she has no proof in the verse, for two reasons: first, it was revealed concerning calling the disbelievers to faith; second, it only negates that the Prophet himself would be the one to make them hear, and God has spoken truly, for none can make them hear when He wills except Him."]

Qatadah said: "God revived them for him so that they heard his speech as a rebuke, a reproach, and a punishment."

The view of the scholars is the soundness of Ibn 'Umar's report, because it has many supporting corroborations confirming its authenticity. Among the most famous is what Ibn 'Abd al-Barr transmitted, authenticating it, from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet ﷺ: "There is no one who passes by the grave of his Muslim brother, whom he knew in this world, and greets him, except that God returns his spirit to him until he returns the greeting."

[Al-Istidhkar of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, through Bishr ibn Bukayr, from al-Awza'i, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet. Its wording: "There is no one who passes by the grave of his believing brother, whom he knew in this world, and greets him, except that he recognizes him and returns the greeting."]

It is established from him ﷺ that the dead hears the sound of the sandals of those who accompany him when they turn away from him. The Prophet ﷺ prescribed for his community that when they greet the people of the graves, they should greet them with the greeting one addresses to someone who can hear, saying: "Peace be upon you, abode of a believing people." This is an address to one who hears and understands. Were it not for this address, they would be like one addressed when non-existent or inanimate. The early righteous Muslims (al-Salaf) agree on this, and reports from them are widespread that the dead recognize the visit of the living to them and rejoice in it. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in his book "al-Qubur" from 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No man visits the grave of his brother and sits beside it, except that he is comforted by him and returns his greeting until he stands up."

It was narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: "When a man passes by a grave he knows and greets it, the one within returns the greeting."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated with his chain from a man of the family of 'Asim al-Jahdari, who said: I saw 'Asim al-Jahdari in my dream two years after his death. I said: "Did you not die?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Where are you?" He said: "I am, by God, in a garden of the gardens of Paradise, I and a group of my companions. We gather every Friday night and Friday morning at Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani, and we receive news of you." I said: "Are your bodies or your spirits?" He said: "Far from it! The bodies have decayed; only the spirits meet." I said: "Do you know of our visiting you?" He said: "We know of it on Friday evening, all of Friday, and Saturday until sunrise." I said: "How is that, rather than all the days?" He said: "Because of the excellence and greatness of Friday."

He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Bakr ibn Muhammad told us: Hasan al-Qassab told us: "I used to go out every Saturday morning with Muhammad ibn Wasi' until we came to the people of al-Jabban (the cemetery). We would stand at the graves, greet them, and pray for them, then leave. One day I said: 'What if we made this day Monday instead?' He said: 'It has reached me that the dead know of their visitors on Friday, and on the day before it, and the day after it.'" He said: Muhammad told us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Aban told us: Sufyan al-Thawri told us: "It reached me from al-Dahhak that he said: Whoever visits a grave on Saturday before sunrise, the dead person knows of his visit." It was asked: "How is that?" He said: "Because of the status of Friday."

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman told us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: Mutarrif used to go out, and when it was Friday he would travel by night. He said: I also heard Abu al-Tayyah say: "It reached us that he used to stay at Ghawtah, and one night he came, and when he reached the graves he stood on his horse. He saw the people of the graves, each occupant sitting on his grave. They said: 'This is Mutarrif, who comes on Friday, and they pray beside you on Friday?' They said: 'Yes, and we know what the birds say about him.' I said: 'And what do they say?' He said: 'They say: Peace be upon you.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us: al-Fadl ibn al-Muwaffaq, the maternal uncle of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, told us: "When my father died, I grieved over him intensely, and I used to visit his grave every day. Then I reduced that for as long as God willed. Then one day I went to him, and while I was sitting by the grave my eyes overcame me and I slept. I saw as if my father's grave had split open, and he was sitting in his grave wrapped in his shroud, with the pallor of the dead upon him." He said: "I wept when I saw him." He said: "O my son, what delayed you from me?" I said: "Do you know of my coming?" He said: "You have never come once except that I knew it. You used to come to me, and I was delighted by you, and those around me were delighted by your prayers." He said: "I then used to visit him often after that."

Muhammad narrated to me: Yahya ibn Bistam told us: 'Uthman ibn Suwayd al-Tufawi told us: "His mother was one of the devout women, and she was called 'the nun'. When she was dying she raised her head to the sky and said: 'O my treasure and my store, on whom I rely in my life and after my death, do not forsake me at death and do not make me lonely.' Then she died. I used to visit her every Friday, pray for her, ask forgiveness for her and for the people of the graves. Then one day I saw her in my dream, and I said to her: 'O my mother, how are you?' She said: 'O my son, death has a severe distress, but I am, praise be to God, in a pleasant barzakh, where fragrant plants are spread out for us, and we rest on silk and brocade until the Day of Resurrection.' I said to her: 'Do you have a need?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Do not abandon what you used to do of visiting us and praying for us, for I am told of your coming on Friday when you come from your family. It is said to me: O Raahibah, this is your son, who has come. So I rejoice, and those among the dead around me rejoice with me.'"

Muhammad narrated to me: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Sulayman told us: Bishr ibn Mansur told us: "In the time of the plague, a man used to frequent the cemetery and attend the funeral prayers. When evening came he would stand at the graves and say: 'May God comfort your loneliness, have mercy on your strangeness, overlook your evildoers, and accept your good deeds,' and he would add nothing to these words. He said: One night I came in the evening and went home to my family without going to the graves to pray as I used to. While I was sleeping, behold, a group of people came to me. I said: 'Who are you and what do you need?' They said: 'We are the people of the graves.' I said: 'What do you need?' They said: 'You have accustomed us to a gift from you when you turn to your family.' I said: 'And what is it?' They said: 'The supplications you used to make.' I said: 'I will return to that.' He said: 'I never abandoned them afterward.'"

More than that, the dead know the deeds of the living among their relatives and brothers. 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ibrahim, from Ayyub, who said: "The deeds of the living are presented to the dead. If they see good, they rejoice and are delighted, and if they see evil, they say: 'O God, turn it back.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawwari, who said: Muhammad, my brother, told us: "'Abbad ibn 'Abbad entered upon Ibrahim ibn Salih, who was in Palestine, and said: 'Advise me.' He said: 'What shall I advise you with, may God set you right? It has reached me that the deeds of the living are presented to their dead relatives. So look at what is presented to the Messenger of God ﷺ of your deeds.' Ibrahim wept until his beard was soaked." Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me: Khalid ibn 'Amr al-Umawi told us: Sadaqah ibn Sulayman al-Ja'fari told us: "I had a shameful, ugly behavior. Then my father died, and I repented and regretted what I had neglected. Then I slipped into a severe slip, and I saw my father in a dream. He said: 'O my son, how great was my joy in you, when your deeds were presented to us, and we compared them with the deeds of the righteous. But this time, I am greatly ashamed because of it, so do not disgrace me among those around me of the dead.'" He said: "After that I used to hear him in his supplication at dawn, and he was my neighbor in Kufa, saying: 'I ask You for a return from which there is no turning back, nor deviation. O Corrector of the righteous, O Guide of the misguided, O Most Merciful of the merciful.'"

This is a topic on which there are many reports from the Companions. Some of the Ansar, relatives of 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, used to say: "O God, I seek refuge in You from a deed by which I would be disgraced before 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah," and he would say this after 'Abdullah had been martyred.

It has been legislated to greet the dead with peace, and greeting with peace one who neither perceives nor knows the one greeting is impossible. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught his community that when they see graves they should say: "Peace be upon you, O abode of believers. Indeed, we, if Allah wills, will be joining you. May Allah have mercy on those of us who went before and those who come after. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you." So this greeting, address and call are directed to an existing being who hears, is addressed, understands and responds, even if the one greeting does not hear the response. And Allah knows best.

It was narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: "When a man passes by a grave he knows and greets it, the one within returns the greeting."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated with his chain from a man of the family of 'Asim al-Jahdari, who said: I saw 'Asim al-Jahdari in my dream two years after his death. I said: "Did you not die?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Where are you?" He said: "I am, by God, in a garden of the gardens of Paradise, I and a group of my companions. We gather every Friday night and Friday morning at Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani, and we receive news of you." I said: "Are your bodies or your spirits?" He said: "Far from it! The bodies have decayed; only the spirits meet." I said: "Do you know of our visiting you?" He said: "We know of it on Friday evening, all of Friday, and Saturday until sunrise." I said: "How is that, rather than all the days?" He said: "Because of the excellence and greatness of Friday."

He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Bakr ibn Muhammad told us: Hasan al-Qassab told us: "I used to go out every Saturday morning with Muhammad ibn Wasi' until we came to the people of al-Jabban (the cemetery). We would stand at the graves, greet them, and pray for them, then leave. One day I said: 'What if we made this day Monday instead?' He said: 'It has reached me that the dead know of their visitors on Friday, and on the day before it, and the day after it.'" He said: Muhammad told us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Aban told us: Sufyan al-Thawri told us: "It reached me from al-Dahhak that he said: Whoever visits a grave on Saturday before sunrise, the dead person knows of his visit." It was asked: "How is that?" He said: "Because of the status of Friday."

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman told us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: Mutarrif used to go out, and when it was Friday he would travel by night. He said: I also heard Abu al-Tayyah say: "It reached us that he used to stay at Ghawtah, and one night he came, and when he reached the graves he stood on his horse. He saw the people of the graves, each occupant sitting on his grave. They said: 'This is Mutarrif, who comes on Friday, and they pray beside you on Friday?' They said: 'Yes, and we know what the birds say about him.' I said: 'And what do they say?' He said: 'They say: Peace be upon you.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us: al-Fadl ibn al-Muwaffaq, the maternal uncle of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, told us: "When my father died, I grieved over him intensely, and I used to visit his grave every day. Then I reduced that for as long as God willed. Then one day I went to him, and while I was sitting by the grave my eyes overcame me and I slept. I saw as if my father's grave had split open, and he was sitting in his grave wrapped in his shroud, with the pallor of the dead upon him." He said: "I wept when I saw him." He said: "O my son, what delayed you from me?" I said: "Do you know of my coming?" He said: "You have never come once except that I knew it. You used to come to me, and I was delighted by you, and those around me were delighted by your prayers." He said: "I then used to visit him often after that."

Muhammad narrated to me: Yahya ibn Bistam told us: 'Uthman ibn Suwayd al-Tufawi told us: "His mother was one of the devout women, and she was called 'the nun'. When she was dying she raised her head to the sky and said: 'O my treasure and my store, on whom I rely in my life and after my death, do not forsake me at death and do not make me lonely.' Then she died. I used to visit her every Friday, pray for her, ask forgiveness for her and for the people of the graves. Then one day I saw her in my dream, and I said to her: 'O my mother, how are you?' She said: 'O my son, death has a severe distress, but I am, praise be to God, in a pleasant barzakh, where fragrant plants are spread out for us, and we rest on silk and brocade until the Day of Resurrection.' I said to her: 'Do you have a need?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Do not abandon what you used to do of visiting us and praying for us, for I am told of your coming on Friday when you come from your family. It is said to me: O Raahibah, this is your son, who has come. So I rejoice, and those among the dead around me rejoice with me.'"

Muhammad narrated to me: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Sulayman told us: Bishr ibn Mansur told us: "In the time of the plague, a man used to frequent the cemetery and attend the funeral prayers. When evening came he would stand at the graves and say: 'May God comfort your loneliness, have mercy on your strangeness, overlook your evildoers, and accept your good deeds,' and he would add nothing to these words. He said: One night I came in the evening and went home to my family without going to the graves to pray as I used to. While I was sleeping, behold, a group of people came to me. I said: 'Who are you and what do you need?' They said: 'We are the people of the graves.' I said: 'What do you need?' They said: 'You have accustomed us to a gift from you when you turn to your family.' I said: 'And what is it?' They said: 'The supplications you used to make.' I said: 'I will return to that.' He said: 'I never abandoned them afterward.'"

More than that, the dead know the deeds of the living among their relatives and brothers. 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ibrahim, from Ayyub, who said: "The deeds of the living are presented to the dead. If they see good, they rejoice and are delighted, and if they see evil, they say: 'O God, turn it back.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawwari, who said: Muhammad, my brother, told us: "'Abbad ibn 'Abbad entered upon Ibrahim ibn Salih, who was in Palestine, and said: 'Advise me.' He said: 'What shall I advise you with, may God set you right? It has reached me that the deeds of the living are presented to their dead relatives. So look at what is presented to the Messenger of God ﷺ of your deeds.' Ibrahim wept until his beard was soaked." Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me: Khalid ibn 'Amr al-Umawi told us: Sadaqah ibn Sulayman al-Ja'fari told us: "I had a shameful, ugly behavior. Then my father died, and I repented and regretted what I had neglected. Then I slipped into a severe slip, and I saw my father in a dream. He said: 'O my son, how great was my joy in you, when your deeds were presented to us, and we compared them with the deeds of the righteous. But this time, I am greatly ashamed because of it, so do not disgrace me among those around me of the dead.'" He said: "After that I used to hear him in his supplication at dawn, and he was my neighbor in Kufa, saying: 'I ask You for a return from which there is no turning back, nor deviation. O Corrector of the righteous, O Guide of the misguided, O Most Merciful of the merciful.'"

This is a topic on which there are many reports from the Companions. Some of the Ansar, relatives of 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, used to say: "O God, I seek refuge in You from a deed by which I would be disgraced before 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah," and he would say this after 'Abdullah had been martyred.

It has been legislated to greet the dead with peace, and greeting with peace one who neither perceives nor knows the one greeting is impossible. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught his community that when they see graves they should say: "Peace be upon you, O abode of believers. Indeed, we, if Allah wills, will be joining you. May Allah have mercy on those of us who went before and those who come after. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you." So this greeting, address and call are directed to an existing being who hears, is addressed, understands and responds, even if the one greeting does not hear the response. And Allah knows best.

Allah draws attention to the human being's passage through the stages of creation, one state after another. His origin is from dust, then from a drop (nutfah), then from a clinging clot ('alaqah), then from a lump of flesh (mudghah), then he becomes bones, then he is clothed with flesh, and the soul is breathed into him. Then he comes out from his mother's womb weak, frail, and feeble in strength. Then he grows gradually little by little until he becomes a child, then a young boy (hadath), then an adolescent (murahiq), then a youth (shabb). This is strength after weakness. Then he begins to decline, so he reaches middle age (yaktahil), then he grows old (yashikh), then he becomes decrepit (yahrim), and this is weakness after strength. Ambition, movement, and force weaken, the hair turns grey (tashibu al-lammah), and the outward and inward attributes change. For this reason He said: ﴿Then He made after strength weakness and grey hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.﴾ That is: He does what He wills and disposes of His servants as He desires, ﴿and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Fudayl and Yazid, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, who said: I recited to Ibn 'Umar: ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness﴾, and he said: ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness﴾. Then he said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as you have recited to me, and he took hold of me as I have taken hold of you.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan) also narrated it from the hadith of Fudayl, with the same chain. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Jabir, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, in similar wording.

Allah, the Exalted, informs us of the ignorance of the disbelievers in this world and the Hereafter. In this world they did what they did, worshipping idols. In the Hereafter, great ignorance will also come from them. Among it is their swearing by Allah that they did not remain in the world except for a single hour. Their aim in this is to avoid the establishment of proof against them, and to claim that they were not given respite so that an excuse could be presented to them.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Thus they were ever deluded.﴾ ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: "You have indeed remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection."﴾ That is, the believing scholars will answer them in the Hereafter, just as they established Allah's proof against them in this world. So when they swear that they remained only an hour, they will say to them: ﴿"You have indeed remained in the Book of Allah"﴾, that is, in the Book of Deeds, ﴿"until the Day of Resurrection"﴾, that is, from the day you were created until the day you were raised. ﴿"But you were not knowing."﴾

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So on that Day﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾, that is, [their excuse will not benefit them] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] their apology for what they did, ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends.﴾ That is, they will not be returned to the world. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they should ask to be reconciled, they would not be among those reconciled.﴾ [Fussilat: 24]

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, meaning: We have made the truth clear to them, explained it, and set out for them in it examples so that they might discern the truth and follow it. ﴿And if you brought them a sign, those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are but falsifiers"﴾, meaning: even if they saw any sign whatsoever, whether it was one they had proposed or another, they would not believe in it, and they would consider it magic and falsehood, as they said about the splitting of the moon and similar things. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]. For this reason He said here: ﴿Thus Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know. So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾, meaning: be patient with their opposition and obstinacy, for Allah the Exalted will certainly fulfil for you what He promised you of His help, and of making the final outcome yours and that of those who follow you, in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you uneasy﴾, meaning: rather, remain steadfast in what Allah has sent you with, for it is the truth about which there is no doubt. Do not turn away from it, for there is no guidance to be followed in anything other than it; rather, all truth is confined to it.

Sa'id reported from Qatadah: a man from the Khawarij (Kharijites, an early dissenting sect) called out to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was in prayer, the dawn prayer, saying: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65]. Ali remained silent until he understood what the man had said, and then he answered him while still in prayer with: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And let not those who have no certainty make you uneasy﴾. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir also narrated it by another route, saying:

Ibn WakI' related to us: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Sharik, from Uthman ibn Abi Zur'ah, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: A man from the Khawarij called out to Ali while he was in the dawn prayer, saying: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers"﴾. Ali answered him, while in the prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you uneasy﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/38)].

Another route: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us, Sharik informed us, from Imran ibn Zabyan, from Abu Tahya, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, prayed the dawn prayer, and a man from the Khawarij called out to him: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers﴾. Ali answered him, while in the prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you uneasy﴾.

[What has been related concerning the merit of this noble surah, and the recommendation of reciting it in the dawn prayer]:

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'bah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said: I heard Shabib, Abu Rawh, narrate from a man of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in the dawn prayer, and in it he recited [Surat ar-Rum] and became confused, so he said: "The Qur'an has been confused for us, for some people among you pray with us but do not perform wudu' well. Whoever attends the prayer with us, let him perform wudu' well." [Al-Musnad (3/471)].

This chain is sound (hasan) and the text is sound, and in it there is a remarkable secret and a strange report: that he (peace be upon him) was affected by the deficiency in the wudu' of those who prayed behind him, which indicates that the prayer of the follower is linked to the prayer of the imam.

[End of the commentary on Surat "ar-Rum"]
